concepts.name: SAARC: Founding, Membership and Charter Basics
key_dimensions: Year of establishment (1985, Dhaka) vs. year of Charter signing — common confusion point
Original 7 founding members vs. current 8 members (Afghanistan added in 2007)
Distinction between SAARC members, Observers (9 observers including USA, China, EU) and their voting rights
UPSC trap: Afghanistan's membership status amid Taliban takeover and suspended participation

concepts.name: SAARC Charter: Principles and Prohibited Areas
key_dimensions: Core principle of sovereign equality and non-interference in internal affairs
Explicit prohibition on bilateral and contentious issues being raised in SAARC forums — key structural limitation
Consensus-based decision-making and how it acts as a veto mechanism (India-Pakistan dynamic)
Comparison with ASEAN Charter to highlight difference in dispute-resolution mechanisms

concepts.name: SAARC Summits: Frequency, Suspension and Significance
key_dimensions: Mandatory annual summit rule vs. reality of irregular summits — gap between charter and practice
19th Summit (Islamabad, 2016) cancelled after Uri attack — India and other members boycotted, setting a precedent
Role of summit cancellation as a diplomatic tool and its implications for regional integration
UPSC trap: No formal mechanism to expel a member or suspend a summit under the Charter

concepts.name: SAARC Secretariat: Structure, Location and Role
key_dimensions: Location: Kathmandu, Nepal — frequently asked
Secretary-General: appointed by rotation among member states in alphabetical order for 3-year term
Distinction between Secretariat's administrative role vs. policy-making role (Secretariat cannot initiate policy)
Funding mechanism: contributions proportional to GDP — India as largest contributor

concepts.name: SAFTA: South Asian Free Trade Area — Architecture and Limitations
key_dimensions: Signed in 2004 (Islamabad Summit), entered into force January 2006 — dates are frequently tested
Sensitive Lists: each country maintains a list of products excluded from tariff reduction — major loophole
Difference between SAFTA (goods only) vs. absence of a comparable services/investment framework
UPSC trap: SAFTA does not cover Non-Tariff Barriers (NTBs) which are the real trade impediments in South Asia

concepts.name: SAARC Preferential Trading Arrangement (SAPTA) vs. SAFTA
key_dimensions: SAPTA signed 1993, in force 1995 — precursor to SAFTA, covers limited product-specific tariff concessions
Key difference: SAPTA = preferential tariff on selected goods; SAFTA = free trade area with zero/low tariffs on most goods
Why SAPTA was insufficient: product-by-product negotiation approach made it slow and limited
UPSC trap: SAPTA is still technically in existence — SAFTA did not formally replace/abrogate SAPTA

concepts.name: Intra-SAARC Trade: Statistics, Potential and Barriers
key_dimensions: Intra-SAARC trade is only ~5% of total trade of member countries — lowest among any regional bloc globally
Contrast with ASEAN (~25%) and EU (~60%) intra-regional trade to highlight SAARC's underperformance
Key barriers: Non-tariff barriers, poor connectivity, political tensions, sensitive lists under SAFTA
World Bank estimates: South Asia trades 20% of its potential — gap between actual and potential trade

concepts.name: SAARC Development Fund (SDF): Purpose and Structure
key_dimensions: Established 2010, headquartered in Thimphu, Bhutan — location frequently tested
Three windows: Social, Economic, and Infrastructure — replaces earlier SAARC Fund for Regional Projects (SFRP)
India as largest contributor; smaller nations' access to infrastructure funding
UPSC trap: SDF is not a multilateral development bank — it cannot raise money from capital markets like ADB or World Bank

concepts.name: SAARC and Energy Cooperation: SAARC Energy Ring
key_dimensions: Concept of a SAARC Energy Ring/Grid proposed to interconnect power grids of all 8 members
Existing bilateral success: India-Bhutan hydropower, India-Nepal power trade vs. absence of multilateral energy grid
BIMSTEC as a competing framework for energy cooperation — often more functional than SAARC
UPSC trap: No formal SAARC Energy Treaty exists; cooperation remains at MoU/bilateral level

concepts.name: SAARC Motor Vehicles Agreement (MVA): Failure and Contrast with BBIN
key_dimensions: SAARC MVA failed because Pakistan refused to sign — consensus rule made it dead on arrival
BBIN MVA (Bangladesh, Bhutan, India, Nepal) signed 2015 as sub-regional workaround — Bhutan later opted out of implementation
Concept of 'variable geometry' or sub-regional groupings as a strategy to bypass SAARC's consensus deadlock
UPSC trap: BBIN is not a SAARC sub-group officially — it is an independent sub-regional initiative

concepts.name: SAARC Observers: Status, List and Strategic Implications
key_dimensions: 9 Observer States: USA, EU, China, Japan, South Korea, Australia, Iran, Mauritius, Myanmar — list frequently tested
China's observer status since 2005 and India's concerns about China gaining full membership
Difference between Observer (can attend summits, cannot vote/veto) and full member rights
UPSC trap: Iran is an observer despite not being geographically contiguous — challenges the 'South Asian' identity of SAARC

concepts.name: SAARC vs. BIMSTEC: Comparative Analysis and India's Strategic Shift
key_dimensions: BIMSTEC: 7 members (5 SAARC + Myanmar + Thailand), Bay of Bengal focus, does not include Pakistan
India's strategic pivot from SAARC to BIMSTEC post-2016 Uri attack — BIMSTEC summit used for SAARC-level outreach
Key difference: BIMSTEC has no consensus rule and has sector-specific lead country mechanism
UPSC trap: All SAARC members are not in BIMSTEC (Pakistan, Afghanistan, Maldives are absent) — overlap is partial

concepts.name: SAARC Social Charter and Human Development Agenda
key_dimensions: SAARC Social Charter (2004) — commitments on poverty eradication, health, education, gender equality
SAARC as a platform for non-economic cooperation: disaster management, climate, culture
SAARC Disaster Management Centre (SDMC) — New Delhi, and its limited operational effectiveness
UPSC trap: SAARC Social Charter is legally non-binding — it is a framework document, not an enforceable treaty

concepts.name: SAARC Agreement on Trade in Services (SATIS)
key_dimensions: SATIS signed at 16th Summit (Thimphu, 2010) — extends SAFTA framework to services sector
Based on GATS-positive list approach: members only liberalize services they explicitly list
Implementation has been near-zero due to political tensions and lack of trust
UPSC trap: SATIS covers trade in services but excludes labor mobility — a major gap for South Asia given its demographic dividend

concepts.name: SAARC Regional Connectivity: Corridors, Railways and Waterways
key_dimensions: Proposed SAARC Regional Multimodal Transport Study (SRMTS) — identifies key corridors including road and rail links
India's neighbourhood connectivity initiatives (Maitri Bridge, integrated check posts) bypassing SAARC framework
Pakistan's refusal to grant India Most Favoured Nation (MFN) status — blocks land transit and connectivity
UPSC trap: India granted MFN to Pakistan in 1996 under WTO obligations, but Pakistan never reciprocated — asymmetric MFN situation

concepts.name: SAARC University and People-to-People Initiatives
key_dimensions: South Asian University (SAU): established by SAARC, located in New Delhi, India — operational since 2010
SAARC Cultural Centre: Colombo, Sri Lanka — promotes cultural exchanges
SAARC Visa Exemption Scheme: limited to specific categories (dignitaries, judges, parliamentarians, businesspersons) — not open to general public
UPSC trap: SAARC Visa Exemption Scheme does NOT apply to ordinary citizens — it covers only ~24 specified categories

concepts.name: Pakistan Factor: Structural Impediment to SAARC's Effectiveness
key_dimensions: Consensus rule means India-Pakistan bilateral tensions can paralyze all SAARC decisions
Pakistan's refusal of MFN to India, blocking of MVA, land transit rights — cascading effects on regional integration
Asymmetry: India accounts for ~80% of South Asia's GDP, making it a reluctant hegemon vs. Pakistan's balancing strategy
UPSC trap: The issue is not just bilateral — smaller members like Nepal, Bangladesh lose connectivity benefits due to India-Pakistan deadlock

concepts.name: SAARC and Climate Change/Disaster Risk: Institutional Mechanisms
key_dimensions: SAARC Environment Ministers' Meeting as a platform for climate dialogue
SAARC Coastal Zone Management Centre (Male, Maldives) — focuses on small island and coastal states
SAARC Meteorological Research Centre (Dhaka, Bangladesh) — early warning systems
UPSC trap: Multiple SAARC specialized centres exist in different member countries — location-based questions are common; e.g., Forestry Centre in Thimphu, TB Centre in Kathmandu

concepts.name: SAARC's Place in India's Neighbourhood First Policy
key_dimensions: Neighbourhood First Policy launched 2014 — SAARC summit in Kathmandu was PM Modi's first multilateral engagement
Tension between Neighbourhood First rhetoric and practical bypassing of SAARC through bilateral deals
India's use of sub-regional formats (BBIN, BIMSTEC, IORA) as functional alternatives to SAARC
UPSC trap: Neighbourhood First Policy includes Myanmar and beyond — not limited to SAARC members, unlike SAARC's geographic scope

concepts.name: SAARC Specialized Bodies and Apex Institutions: Roles and Locations
key_dimensions: Distinction between SAARC Recognized Bodies (professional associations), SAARC Regional Centres and SAARC Apex Bodies
Key centres: SAARC Agriculture Centre (Dhaka), SAARC Documentation Centre (New Delhi), SAARC Human Resource Development Centre (Islamabad)
SAARC Finance Ministers' and Central Bank Governors' meetings — coordination on macroeconomic issues
UPSC trap: SAARC Finance Governors' mechanism is not equivalent to a monetary union or currency arrangement — purely consultative
